passages.note: Aye on Assembly concurrence in Senate amendments, the final Assembly vote on the chaptered text; 16 of 77 voting No, so not near-unanimous.

passages.provision_quote: shall not enact or enforce any policy, rule, or administrative regulation that would require an employee or a contractor to disclose any information related to a pupil’s sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression to any other person without the pupil’s consent, unless otherwise required by state or federal law.
passages.note: Operative Section 220.5(a) forbids local rules requiring disclosure without the pupil's consent; it does not require staff to withhold (so not rung 1), and the forbidding of such rules is itself the rung's clause, so this is not mere preemption.

rows.reasoning: Gabriel voted Aye on final Assembly passage (concurrence, 61-16) of AB 1955, a single-subject pupil-rights bill whose operative Section 220.5(a) bars schools and boards from enacting or enforcing any policy that would require staff to disclose a pupil's gender identity without the pupil's consent. That matches the rung "Forbid rules that require schools to tell parents"; the bill does not require staff to keep identity from parents (excluding the consent-secrecy rung) and requires no notification or permission.
